balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (lease liabilities excluded).

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: most of "Total Debt" is not bank debt -- it is loans from the Luxshare group (HK$3,076.8m of the HK$4,042.7m at H1 FY2026). See the Debt Composition chart below for the split; the DCF's net-debt bridge nets HK$4,852.3m cash against this total (net cash of roughly HK$810m), but related-party debt carries a different renewal/repricing risk than a bank facility.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Whether Luxshare-group loans are rolled over or termed out

debtComposition.title: Debt composition: bank vs Luxshare-group loans
debtComposition.content:
Total debt splits into bank borrowings (arm's-length facilities) and loans from related companies -- funding from the Luxshare Precision Industry group, which is both the controlling shareholder and, via these loans, a lender.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: at H1 FY2026, related-party loans (HK$3,076.8m) were over three times bank borrowings (HK$965.9m) -- up from roughly parity a year earlier. Combined with related-party sales (caps raised to HK$3,497m for 2026, an estimated ~45% of revenue), the Group's financing and its commercial relationships both run through the same controlling party.

What to watch:

  • Whether the mix shifts back toward bank debt as the balance sheet strengthens post-placing
  • Disclosed terms (rate, tenor, security) on the Luxshare-group loans versus bank facilities
  • Concentration risk if Luxshare's own demand or strategy changes

sharePlacing.title: Share placing and dilution
sharePlacing.content:
Share placing proceeds are cash raised from issuing new shares; shares outstanding shows the resulting dilution.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: two placings in H1 FY2026 (Feb 2026, HK$1.63bn, and May 2026, HK$2.88bn) raised roughly HK$4.5bn and lifted the share count from ~1,840m to ~2,232m shares -- about 21% dilution in one half-year, funding M&A, overseas expansion and balance-sheet strengthening (including the swing to net cash). This chart is FY-only because placings are discrete events, not a recurring per-period metric.

What to watch:

  • Per-share metrics (EPS, owner FCF per share) after the enlarged share base annualises
  • Whether further placings follow, or whether this was a one-off deleveraging raise

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Time Interconnect Technology Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
